Tutorial
How to Play Pool
Pool is a game where the player uses a cue stick to strike the white (cue) ball and knock other balls into the pockets.

Banking
Before playing, you must decide who goes first.
Each player strikes the cue ball. The player whose ball stops closest to them goes first.
However, the ball must hit the opposing cushion once in order to be counted.

Shot Controls
Use <Action:Button_RS_Down@Billard> to draw back the cue stick.
Attention should be paid to the degree to which the cue stick is drawn back, as it affects the power of the shot.
Use <Action:Button_RS_Up@Billard> to execute the shot.

Adjusting Shot Angle
First, choose the angle to strike the cue ball.
Use <Action:Button_LS_Up@Billard><Action:Button_LS_Down@Billard><Action:Button_LS_Left@Billard><Action:Button_LS_Right@Billard> to adjust the angle.
In shot mode, <Action:Button_LS_Up@Billard><Action:Button_LS_Down@Billard><Action:Button_LS_Left@Billard><Action:Button_LS_Right@Billard> can be used to adjust the impact point.
Adjusting the impact point puts a spin on the ball. Adjust the impact point as necessary.
How to Play Nine-ball
Pocket the object balls in order, starting with the lowest number, by hitting them with the cue ball.
Your turn continues until you fail to pocket a ball.
The first player to sink the 9 ball wins.
Fouls
A foul results if the cue ball falls into a pocket or does not strike an object ball.
The opposing player may then take a shot by placing the cue ball anywhere on the table.
Now, let's have you try it yourself.
How to Play Eight-ball
Eight-ball uses balls number 1 through 15.
Players must pocket the balls on the table in order, starting with the lowest-numbered ball.
Pocketing a ball awards the player with the same number of points as the ball's number.
The first player to exceed 61 points wins.
Balls 1 through 7 are called Low Balls, while balls 9 through 15 are called High Balls.
The first ball that is pocketed after the break shot determines the group you will be targeting.
To win, you must pocket the 8 ball after pocketing all of the balls in your group.
You can pocket the balls in your group in any order.
When you're ready to pocket the 8 ball, you must specify the pocket that you'll be aiming for.
Sinking it in any other pocket results in an automatic loss.
Pocketing the 8 ball before all of the balls in your group have been sunk also counts as a loss.
Use <Action:Button_RS_Down@Billard> to draw back the cue stick.
The farther back you pull it, the stronger the shot will be.
Moving it straight back towards you is the key to making accurate shots.
That was a fine match! Would you like to play Prize Bank Shot?

Changing Camera Angle
Use <Action:Button_RS_Up@Billard><Action:Button_RS_Down@Billard><Action:Button_RS_Left@Billard><Action:Button_RS_Right@Billard> to change the camera angle while deciding on a striking angle.
Press <Action:Button_Square@Billard>  for an overhead view.
Adjust the camera angle to find the best possible shot angle.

Shooting
After choosing an angle, press <Action:Button_Cross@Billard> to enter shot mode.
Just like before, <Action:Button_RS_Down@Billard> can be used to adjust the power of the shot.
Move it straight towards you to take a steady shot.
